ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the vertical plane coordinate system $x O y$, there is a uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction strength $B$ in the third quadrant, directed horizontally and perpendicularly outward from the paper. There is also a uniform electric field in the negative $x$-axis direction with a field strength of $E{=}1\mathrm{N/C}$. In the first quadrant, there is a uniform electric field in the negative $y$-axis direction with the same field strength $E{=}1\mathrm{N/C}$, and in the region where $y{>}h{=}0.4\mathrm{m}$, there is a uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction strength $B$ directed perpendicularly into the paper. An oil droplet with a charge of $-q$ acquires an initial velocity $v_{0}=2\sqrt{2}\mathrm{m/s}$ from point $P$ in the third quadrant, allowing it to move in a straight line at constant speed along $P O$ (where $P O$ makes an angle of $\theta=45^{\circ}$ with the negative $x$-axis) and enters the first quadrant from the origin $O$. The gravitational acceleration is known to be $g{=}10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction $B$ and the specific charge of the oil droplet?
2. How long does the oil droplet take to move in the first quadrant?
3. What is the $x$ coordinate value when the oil droplet leaves the first quadrant?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the coordinate axes show the x-axis pointing right and the y-axis pointing upward, with O as the origin. In the third quadrant, a leftward horizontal electric field arrow E is drawn, and dots are used to indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper outward; an oil drop moves from point P in the third quadrant along the dashed line PO toward O, with velocity v0 along PO, and the angle between PO and the negative x-axis is marked θ. In the first quadrant, a vertically downward electric field arrow E is drawn; in the region above the dashed horizontal line y=h, crosses are drawn, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper inward. Reasoning: The oil drop's charge is -q, and take q>0. When entering O along PO, θ=45°, so the velocity components are vx=vy=v0 cos45°=2 m/s. In the third quadrant, the oil drop moves in uniform straight-line motion, so the resultant force is zero. The electric field is in the negative x direction, and the electric field force on the negative charge is in the positive x direction; the magnetic field is outward, and the x component of the magnetic force on the negative charge is in the negative x direction, while the y component is in the positive y direction. Thus the equilibrium in the x direction is: qE=qBvy, namely E=Bvy, so B=E/vy=1/2=0.5 T. The equilibrium in the y direction is: qBvx=mg, so q/m=g/(Bvx)=10/(0.5×2)=10 C/kg. Thus qE/m=10 m/s², exactly equal to g. After entering the first quadrant, in the region 0<y<h there is no magnetic field, the electric field is downward, and the electric field force on the negative charge is upward, with magnitude qE; because qE/m=g, the electric field force and gravity cancel, and the velocity remains (2,2). The time to reach y=h=0.4 m is t1=h/vy=0.4/2=0.2 s, and at this time x1=2t1=0.4 m. In the region y>h, the electric field force still cancels gravity, and only the magnetic force acts. The magnetic field above the first quadrant is perpendicular to the paper inward, and for the negative charge the equations of motion are dvx/dt=ωvy, dvy/dt=-ωvx, where ω=(q/m)B=10×0.5=5 s^-1. Taking the moment of entering the magnetic field above y=h as τ=0, the initial velocity is still vx=vy=2, then vx=2cos(ωτ)+2sin(ωτ), vy=2cos(ωτ)-2sin(ωτ). Integrating gives y=h+(2/ω)[sin(ωτ)+cos(ωτ)-1], x=x1+(2/ω)[sin(ωτ)+1-cos(ωτ)]. When the oil drop first returns to the boundary y=h, it leaves the upper magnetic-field region. Take the smallest nonzero solution of sinφ+cosφ-1=0, φ=ωτ=π/2. Therefore τ2=π/(2ω)=π/10≈0.314 s, x2=0.4+(2/5)(1+1)=1.2 m, and at this time the velocity becomes (2,-2). After returning to the region 0<y<h, there is still no magnetic field, and the electric field force and gravity cancel, so the oil drop moves uniformly toward the lower right with velocity (2,-2). The time from y=h to the x-axis is t3=h/2=0.2 s, and x increases again by 2t3=0.4 m. Therefore the total time in the first quadrant is t=t1+τ2+t3=0.2+0.314+0.2≈0.714 s, and when leaving the first quadrant x=1.2+0.4=1.6 m.
